opsmind-incidents.content:
Incident #INC-20261108-6055 Resolution Report:
Service: checkout-service (Severity: P1)
Title: checkout-service: OOMKilled_MemoryStarvation
Symptoms: checkout-service pod memory limits exceeded. 504 Gateway Timeouts.
Confirmed Root Cause: Redis cache eviction policy set to noeviction under high traffic
Applied Resolution: Applied hotfix: config set maxmemory-policy volatile-lru and expanded Redis RAM
Lessons Learned: Never allow noeviction policy in production caching tiers.
Tags: checkout-service, outage-fix, verified-resolution

metadata.root_cause: Redis cache eviction policy set to noeviction under high traffic
metadata.resolution: Applied hotfix: config set maxmemory-policy volatile-lru and expanded Redis RAM

opsmind-services.content: payment-service is a Tier-1 critical service responsible for checkout transactions. Dependencies: redis-cache-cluster (port 6379, session & rate-limiting cache), postgres-db-primary (port 5432). In production, memory limit is 4GiB. Vulnerable to Redis buffer starvation if maxmemory-policy is set to noeviction.

auth-service is a Tier-1 authentication service issuing JWT tokens. Dependencies: redis-sessions (port 6380), ldap-identity-provider. Canary deployments require verification of token validation latency.

opsmind-runbooks.content: Standard Runbook for Redis Connection Pool Exhaustion: 1. Verify active connection count via `redis-cli info clients`. 2. Check Redis memory usage via `redis-cli info memory`. 3. Ensure eviction policy is set to volatile-lru or allkeys-lru. 4. Expand connection pool size or restart stalled pods safely.
Verified Runbook for checkout-service: Applied hotfix: config set maxmemory-policy volatile-lru and expanded Redis RAM
